shortDescription: Brazil's central bank said on Wednesday it will start holding auctions on October 5 to roll over traditional currency swaps maturing on November 3, according to a statement.

children: Brazil's central bank said on Wednesday it will start holding auctions on October 5 to roll over traditional currency swaps maturing on November 3, according to a statement.
The central bank typically uses such operations to provide currency hedging and maintain market liquidity.
In a traditional currency swap, the central bank pays the buyer the currency variation plus an interest rate, and receives the variation in Brazil's Selic rate.
